defiscan.label: Stage 2
defiscan.verbatim: Stage 2. Uniswap v3 is an AMM that builds upon Uniswap v2 by introducing a concentrated liquidity model, providing liquidity providers with granular control over capital allocation. Unlike v2, where liquidity is distributed uniformly across all price ranges, v3 allows LPs to specify custom price ranges in which their liquidity is active. This approach significantly improves capital efficiency, as LPs can concentrate their assets in high-demand price ranges, earning fees only within those specified ranges. Uniswap v3 also introduces multiple fee tiers (0.01%, 0.05%, 0.3%, and 1%) to support different asset volatility profiles, allowing LPs to adjust their fee preferences based on expected risk and return. Additionally, it incorporates "range orders," which effectively turn liquidity positions into limit orders, further enhancing LP strategy flexibility. The protocol is deployed across multiple chains enabling a wide range of use cases across decentralized finance (DeFi) applications. [Partial: DeFiScan covers Uniswap v2/v3; v4 / UniswapX not reviewed as one family entry]

keyFindings.title: EOA controls Arbitrum v4 PoolManager ownership
keyFindings.description: On-chain owner() of Arbitrum UniswapV4 PoolManager (0x360e68faccca8ca495c1b759fd9eee466db9fb32) resolves to 0x2bad8182c09f50c8318d769245bea52c32be46cd, confirmed EOA (eth_getCode empty). This address can call setProtocolFeeController() and transferOwnership() per verified PoolManager source. Single-key compromise could reassign protocol-fee authority or ownership without timelock/multisig protection.

keyFindings.title: Same EOA controls Unichain v2 feeToSetter
keyFindings.description: The same EOA 0x2bad8182c09f50c8318d769245bea52c32be46cd is feeToSetter on Unichain UniswapV2Factory (0x1f9840…002), granting setFeeTo/setFeeToSetter privileges per verified v2 factory source. Cross-chain concentration of privileged roles in one EOA expands blast radius beyond Arbitrum v4.

keyFindings.title: UNI governance Timelock unverified on Etherscan
keyFindings.description: The UNI Timelock at 0x1a9C8182C09F50C8318d769245beA52c32BE35BC is marked unverified in VERIFICATION_STATUS.md with no downloadable source. On-chain it is a live contract (admin=0x408ed6354d4973f66138c91495f2f2fcbd8724c3) and owns Ethereum v4 PoolManager, is V2 feeToSetter, and is UNI minter. Lack of explorer verification prevents independent audit of the governance execution layer controlling protocol-fee and minting paths.

keyFindings.title: Four scoped deployments lack verified explorer source
keyFindings.description: Pipeline verification flags four contracts as unverified: Ethereum NonfungiblePositionManager (0xC36442b4…), Ethereum Timelock (0x1a9C8182…), Optimism UniswapV3Factory (0x1F98431c…), and Base Permit2 (0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3). Unverified bytecode cannot be source-audited via explorer; NPM and Permit2 hold user NFT positions and token approvals respectively, amplifying impact.

keyFindings.title: Arbitrum Admin Controlled by EOA, Not L1 Timelock
keyFindings.description: On Arbitrum, UniswapV3Factory owner (0xff7a…0699) and UniswapV4 PoolManager owner (0x2bad…46cd) both resolve to EOA 0x2bad8182c09f50c8318d769245bea52c32be46cd (verified: code length 0, transaction nonce 8). This EOA can call setOwner on the v3 ProtocolFeeController and transferOwnership on v4 PoolManager without the 2-day Ethereum timelock delay or UNI holder vote. Base and Optimism use bridged L2 admin contracts whose storage slot 1 points to the Ethereum timelock — Arbitrum lacks this linkage.

keyFindings.title: Cross-Chain Governance Asymmetry Across L2s
keyFindings.description: L2 factory/PoolManager admin addresses differ per chain and are not uniformly controlled by the Ethereum timelock. Base/Optimism L2 proxy contracts (1419 bytes) store admin=0x4200…0007 (L2CrossDomainMessenger) and reference L1 timelock 0x1a9C…35BC in storage slot 1, enabling L1-governance relay. Arbitrum uses a standalone EOA. Polygon, BSC, and 35+ other chains listed in discovery have independent deployments with no on-chain linkage to Ethereum governance verified in this analysis.

keyFindings.title: v4 Hook Composability Creates Third-Party Integration Risk
keyFindings.description: v4 PoolManager delegates swap, liquidity, and donate lifecycle to arbitrary IHooks contracts chosen per pool. PoolManager correctly passes msg.sender to hook callbacks and prevents hook self-calls, but does not enforce onlyPoolManager on hook entrypoints—third-party hooks must implement access control themselves. Cork Protocol lost ~$12M (May 2025) when CorkHook.beforeSwap lacked PoolManager-only validation, allowing direct invocation with malicious hookData. Uniswap core was not exploited; the integrating protocol was.

keyFindings.title: v4 hooks delegate execution to arbitrary pool-configured contracts
keyFindings.description: Verified PoolManager source invokes hook contracts at initialize, modifyLiquidity, swap, and donate via before/after hooks with optional delta returns. Core enforces hook-address bit flags but does not constrain hook logic. Poorly implemented or malicious hooks (e.g., Cork Protocol May 2025) can cause LP/user losses while Uniswap core remains technically correct. LPs must audit per-pool hook behavior.

keyFindings.title: Privileged admin addresses diverge across chains
keyFindings.description: Factory/PoolManager owners are not uniform: Ethereum v4 PoolManager owner is UNI Timelock (0x1a9c8182…), Ethereum v3 factory owner is a separate 14.5KB contract (0xf2371551…), while Arbitrum/Base/Optimism v3 owners are chain-local 14.5KB contracts and v4 owners differ (Arbitrum EOA, Base/Optimism 2.8KB contracts). v3/v4 factories also use different addresses on some chains (e.g., Base v3 at 0x33128a8f… vs canonical 0x1F98431c…). Increases risk of integrator misconfiguration and uneven governance protections.

keyFindings.title: Permit2 is immutable and ownerless but aggregates token approvals
keyFindings.description: Verified Permit2 source shows no owner/admin/pause functions — deployment is immutable. Users granting Permit2 max approvals enable signature-based transfers via any integrated router. This is by design but creates a high-value phishing/approval-theft target; Base deployment is additionally unverified on BaseScan despite CREATE2 canonical address.

keyFindings.title: Timelock Contract Source Unverified on Etherscan
keyFindings.description: The UNI timelock at 0x1a9C8182C09F50C8318d769245beA52c32BE35BC has no verified source code on Etherscan. On-chain storage confirms Compound-style layout (admin=Governor Bravo, delay=172800s/2 days), but unverified bytecode prevents independent audit of the full execution logic and queued-transaction handling.

keyFindings.title: UNIfication Restructures Off-Chain Control Under DUNI/Labs
keyFindings.description: The Dec 2025 UNIfication proposal (passed with ~99.9% support) consolidates Uniswap Foundation teams into Uniswap Labs, establishes a Wyoming DUNA (DUNI) legal entity, creates a 20M UNI/year growth budget under a Labs–DUNI service provider agreement, and activates protocol fee switches. On-chain fee parameters remain governable by UNI votes, but operational execution, interface/API fee removal, and legal/regulatory engagement shift toward Labs and DUNI — increasing off-chain centralization relative to pure on-chain DAO control.
